correctness.rationale: The proposed values satisfy the rational equilibrium equations, including the two rate-source balances and P=mu N+aI. Both rate values lie strictly inside admissible clipping intervals, so the auxiliary states and clipped rates agree locally. Independent symbolic differentiation and exact polynomial calculation reproduce both Jacobians and characteristic polynomials. The cubic has positive coefficients and strict Hurwitz margin 1753317/180500000. The full quintic has nonzero Routh pivots with signs (+,+,+,-,+,+), giving exactly two open right-half-plane roots with multiplicity. Since all quintic coefficients are positive, these are a conjugate nonreal pair. Positive real parts establish local instability of the five-state equilibrium, not a Hopf bifurcation.
residual_risks: Local witness only, for the particular simulation feedback laws at an interior equilibrium. No inference about Hopf, nonlinear cycles, arbitrary feedback functions, or the source's own simulation parameter sets.

evidence: Theorem 7 proves its local no-Hopf assertion using a 3×3 Jacobian and a cubic. The general setup permits source functions beyond the simulation choice, without a full-Jacobian result that supplies the witness.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General theory that feedback can destabilize a stable block does not certify instability with the signs, equilibrium constraints and admissible clipping of this model.

value.rationale: An admissible exact counterexample answers whether stable population dynamics at fixed rates can justify endemic stability after including the published feedback.
